info.name: TaskFlow
info.description:
REST API collection for the TaskFlow project (a Jira-like project tracking backend built with NestJS). Covers every REST endpoint with both success and failure scenarios (validation errors, auth/role failures, not-found cases).

**Auth model**: session-cookie based (express-session + passport). Run a "Login" request first — Postman's cookie jar will then automatically attach the session cookie to subsequent requests against the same {{baseUrl}}. Requests marked "not logged in" explicitly disable auth/cookies for that one request via a noauth override, so they still fail correctly even if you are logged in from a previous request.

**Seeded test data**: SeedService assigns @test.com users to projects using a fixed "memberIndices" list per project in test-data/projects.json, so the same users always end up with the same roles on the same projects across every fresh seed. This collection relies on that: testOwnerEmail (James Smith) is always OWNER, and testEditorEmail (Patricia Perez) is always an EDITOR, of the "Project Phoenix" project — used by the "Resolve seeded project id" / "insufficient project role" requests in the Project folder. These emails are derived from committed, non-secret test data, so they're hardcoded as collection variables; only the shared password comes from your own .env (DEFAULT_PASSWORD).

**Setup**: open this collection's Variables tab and fill in the "Current value" column for adminEmail / adminPassword / defaultEmail / defaultPassword to match your local .env seed values. Never commit real values into those fields.

**Issue tracking**: the Issue/Label/Comment folders cover the core "Jira-like" domain. Issues/Labels require OWNER/ADMIN/EDITOR project roles to create or update (OWNER/ADMIN to delete); Comments may be created by any project member, including VIEWER, and edited/deleted by their own author or a project OWNER/ADMIN. SeedService seeds 4 labels and 5 issues per project deterministically (see its source for the exact templates), so Project Phoenix always has the same seeded issues/labels to test against.

Log in as admin first. The level column is stored uppercase ("INFO"/"WARN"/"ERROR") and matched exactly, so the query param must match that case. Seeding deliberately triggers 6 bad requests (duplicate email, password mismatch, missing properties, not-found/invalid-id lookups) specifically so this filter has real WARN rows to return — also try "INFO" (plentiful) or "ERROR" (none from seeding; only real unexpected failures log at this level).
